category_title: Elementary student with Duchenne muscular dystrophy exhibiting task-avoidant and attention-seeking disruptive behaviors
minimal_context: Philip is in the school yard during break time while his classmates are starting a game of soccer.
dialogue:
TUTOR: The bell just rang for break time. You can go out to the school yard now.

STUDENT: (Follows the classmates outside and intrudes on their soccer game, trying to grab the ball to get their attention)

TUTOR: Philip, please let them play their game.

STUDENT: But I want to play! (Stands in the middle of the field, annoying the other children)

TUTOR: You need to figure out how to join in with them.

STUDENT: (Falls on the ground) You didn't invite me to play with you! (Cries loudly and yells at his classmates)

options.A: Reinforce the student with a sticker of his favorite soccer team on a daily basis.
options.B: Provide a clear beginning and end for each break time activity in the school yard.
options.C: Change the entire structure of the break time to keep challenging behaviors down.
options.D: Make regulative discourses visible to the student and unpack what he needs to do during breaks.
